newsitem.title: USA: CBOT oat futures end mostly lower on spec selling.
newsitem.headline: CBOT oat futures end mostly lower on spec selling.

text.p: CBOT oat futures closed lower on speculative selling tied to long liquidation and profit taking after the recent strong rally, traders said.
"Commission house stops were hit and fund selling was in there early. It was overdone and they were taking profits," a trader said.
Oats rallied early this week on a transportation snarl in Canada which led to prospects for a lack of rail shipment of Canadian oats into U.S. deliverable position.
"There are underlying reasons for the strength which are the transportation problems," the trader said.
Traders said Canada has to deal with getting wheat into export position and oat stocks would probably go begging until the wheat export programs have been satisfied.
"There is a perceived problem that oats won't come in from Canada in time for delivery," the trader said. First notice day for deliveries on the CBOT March contracts is slated for Feb 28.

Prudential Securities bought 400,000 bushels of May and sold 400,000 March, traders said. Cargill Investor Services, Produce Grain, Smith Barney and Chicago Corp each sold about 200,000 to 300,000 bushels of the March and May.
Oat futures volume was estimated by CBOT at 3,400 contracts, below Wednesday's tally of 4,284.
Oats closed five cents lower to 3/4 higher, with March down five at $1.80-3/4 per biushel.
